transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’ve just been having a hard time doing normal things lately. It’s probably not as bad as it sounds, but mostly I just stay in my room. I keep wearing the same clothes, and I don’t really… do the stuff I used to, like knitting or journaling or going for walks.

My mom asks me what’s wrong, and I feel bad because I barely have the energy to answer her. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

I… I don’t really know. Maybe a little, but I wouldn’t want to say I’m depressed if that’s not the right word. It’s more like I’m just tired and kind of… not doing much. I’m sorry, is that an okay answer?
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to notice?

Um… I don’t think so. Not really, I mean. I haven’t noticed anything like… seeing things, I guess. Hearing things, I’m not sure what would count. Sometimes I get kind of distracted, but I don’t think it’s that.

Is that… is that helpful?
Have you been feeling sad most days?

I’m not sure… I mean, I don’t think I’m sad most days exactly. It’s more like I’m kind of blank or tired, if that makes sense. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have, kind of. I don’t really do the things I used to do anymore, like knitting or writing in my journal, or even going for walks. Mostly I just stay in my room, and sometimes I don’t even change clothes. It sounds bad when I say it like that, sorry. I just can’t really make myself start anything, and when my mom asks what’s wrong I don’t have much energy to answer her. Is that what you mean by losing interest?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?
I don’t think so… not a lot, anyway. I mean, I get nervous sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying all the time for no reason. Or maybe I don’t notice it that way. Is that okay?
Have you had the feeling that your thoughts are being controlled by someone or something outside of you?

Um… controlled, I don’t know if I’d say it exactly like that. Not like someone is moving my thoughts around, I guess. But since I was in those college classes, I’ve felt like the school portal and the clinic practicum people were… sort of sending messages through little wording changes. Like in emails or comments on assignments, it felt like they were marking me as someone they didn’t want in healthcare.

My mom says they’re just normal messages, and maybe that’s what you mean, like maybe I’m reading too much into it. I don’t want to sound dramatic. But it did feel like something outside of me was kind of directing what I was supposed to understand, if that makes sense.
Do you believe those messages really were aimed at you?

I… yeah. I mean, I know my mom says they were just regular emails or normal assignment comments, and I don’t want to seem like I’m making a big thing out of it. But it really did feel aimed at me.

Like the little wording changes in the school portal, or what the clinic practicum people wrote… it felt like they were marking me as someone they didn’t want in healthcare. I know that probably sounds strange, but to me it wasn’t random. It felt like it was about me.
Have you heard voices when no one was there?

I don’t think so… not like a voice in the room or anything. Sometimes I’m not sure what counts, like if I’m really stressed and my thoughts feel loud, but I haven’t noticed hearing someone talking when nobody’s there. Is that what you mean?
Do you still believe those emails and assignment comments were meant to send you messages about not belonging in healthcare?

I mean… yes, I still kind of believe that. I know that probably isn’t the answer I’m supposed to give, and I don’t want to seem difficult, but it still feels like those emails and the comments weren’t just normal.

It’s the little wording changes, like on the portal or in the assignment feedback, and the way the clinic practicum people wrote things. It felt like they were signaling that I wasn’t wanted in healthcare. My mom keeps saying they were just regular messages, and I try to consider that, but… I still feel like they were meant for me.
Do you believe for certain that those emails and assignment comments were intentionally sending you messages about not belonging in healthcare?

I… I don’t want to say it in a way that sounds bad, but yes. It feels certain to me.

Since I was in those college classes, it’s felt like the school portal and the clinic practicum people were using these little wording changes in emails and assignment comments to mark me, like… as someone they don’t want in healthcare. I know my mom says they’re just regular messages, and I try to listen to that, but I still know it was meant that way.
About how long have you been feeling certain that the emails and assignment comments were sending you messages about not belonging in healthcare?

Um… I think it’s been about two months that it’s felt really fixed like that. Maybe it started feeling weird before, but being certain that the portal and the practicum emails were kind of marking me… about the past two months. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
For at least two weeks during this time, have you felt depressed or down most of the day nearly every day?

I’m… not really sure. I mean, I’ve definitely been upset and stressed, but I don’t know if I’d say depressed most of the day nearly every day for two weeks. I don’t want to answer it wrong. It’s more like… I’ve had bad days, but I haven’t really tracked it that way.
During the past two months, have you had a period when you felt down or depressed nearly every day?

I don’t think so… not nearly every day. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt really low or overwhelmed, but I don’t want to exaggerate it. It wasn’t like every day for a whole stretch, at least not that I’m sure of. Does that make sense?
During the past two months, was there a period of at least two weeks when you had almost no interest or enjoyment in things nearly every day?

Yeah… I guess maybe yes. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but mostly I just can’t make myself do things anymore. I kind of stay in my room in the same clothes, and I haven’t really been knitting or journaling or going on walks like I used to. When my mom asks what’s wrong, I barely have the energy to answer her. So… that probably counts, right?
Have you had this belief about the emails and portal messages at times when you were not feeling depressed?

Yes… I think so. I mean, it’s not only when I’m feeling low. Since I was in those college classes, I’ve felt like the school portal and the clinic practicum people were… using little wording changes in emails or assignment comments to sort of mark me, like they didn’t want me in healthcare.

I know my mom says they’re just normal messages, and maybe I’m overreading it, I don’t want to sound dramatic. But it still felt that way even when I wasn’t especially depressed.
Before these past two months, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had sad times before, like anyone, but I don’t know if it was most of the day nearly every day for a full two weeks. I don’t want to say yes if that’s not accurate. So… I think probably not, or at least I can’t remember a time like that clearly.
For at least one month, have you been feeling certain that the emails and assignment comments were sending you messages about not belonging in healthcare?

Yeah… for at least a month, yes. I know it probably sounds like I’m reading too much into things, and I’m not trying to be difficult, but since I was in those classes it felt really clear to me that the portal messages and assignment comments had these little wording changes that meant something. Like they were marking me as someone they didn’t want in healthcare.

My mom keeps saying they’re just regular emails, and maybe that’s what you’d say too, but it didn’t feel regular to me. I felt pretty certain about it.
Have you felt down or depressed more days than not for at least two years?

Um… I don’t think so. I’ve had times where I felt down, but two years sounds like a really long time, and I don’t think it’s been like that more days than not. At least, not that I’ve noticed clearly. Is that… does that answer it okay?
Since these problems started, have you been doing worse at school or work than you were before?

Yeah… I guess I have been doing worse. I don’t want to make it sound like I just gave up, because I was really trying, but I had to stop moving forward in the certificate program. And I’m not really able to handle the practicum right now, or plan for the clinic office job I was working toward.

I know that probably sounds bad… but yes, compared to before, I’m not managing school and the work plans the same way.

patient.answer: Um… I don’t think so. I’ve had times where I felt down, but two years sounds like a really long time, and I don’t think it’s been like that more days than not. At least, not that I’ve noticed clearly. Is that… does that answer it okay?

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been functional decline consistent with schizophrenia rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Since these problems started, have you been doing worse at school or work than you were before?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I had to stop moving forward in the certificate program, and I’m not able to handle the practicum or plan for the clinic office job I was working toward.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the problems have caused decline in school or work functioning, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I guess I have been doing worse. I don’t want to make it sound like I just gave up, because I was really trying, but I had to stop moving forward in the certificate program. And I’m not really able to handle the practicum right now, or plan for the clinic office job I was working toward.

I know that probably sounds bad… but yes, compared to before, I’m not managing school and the work plans the same way.

inference.note: Functional decline with at least 1 month of fixed delusional belief supports a primary psychotic disorder; F34.1 is ruled out by denial of depressed mood more days than not for 2 years. Psychotic depression codes remain possible but less favored because delusion occurs outside clearly depressed periods and sustained depressed mood is not established.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a fixed delusional belief of referential/persecutory type lasting about two months, present with conviction and outside of mood episodes, along with negative-symptom-like deterioration (social withdrawal, reduced activity, poor self-care, low energy) and functional decline in school/work. Criteria for major depressive episode are not clearly met because she denies sustained depressed mood and only anhedonia is clearly established; psychotic depression is therefore less supported. Psychotic symptoms persisting when not depressed and overall decline favor schizophrenia over depressive disorders with psychotic features.
